items.stem: What does the AWS CDK ultimately produce to provision resources?

options.text: CloudFormation templates that CDK synthesizes and deploys
options.rationale: Correct: CDK synthesizes to CloudFormation, which provisions the resources.

options.text: Direct API calls that bypass CloudFormation
options.rationale: CDK deploys through CloudFormation, it does not bypass it.
CDK produces CloudFormation, not Terraform HCL.

options.text: Shell scripts run on each instance
options.rationale: CDK does not provision through per-instance shell scripts.

items.explanation: Correct: CDK synthesizes to CloudFormation templates for deployment.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when working with the AWS CDK? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Review cdk diff before deploying changes
options.rationale: Correct: reviewing the diff prevents unexpected or destructive changes.

options.text: Grant least-privilege IAM via construct grant methods
options.rationale: Correct: grant methods produce scoped, least-privilege policies.

options.text: Hardcode ARNs across stacks instead of passing references
options.rationale: Hardcoding ARNs is brittle; references are preferred.

options.text: Deploy straight to production without any tests
options.rationale: Skipping tests risks shipping broken infrastructure.

items.explanation: Correct: reviewing diffs and using least-privilege grants are CDK best practices.

items.stem: Before cdk deploy, which command shows what will change in the stack?

options.rationale: Correct: cdk diff compares the synthesized template against the deployed stack.
cdk init scaffolds a new project, it does not show changes.
cdk destroy tears down a stack rather than previewing changes.
cdk docs opens documentation, not a change preview.

items.explanation: Correct: cdk diff previews the changes a deploy would make.
